name: Mercury
atmospheric_composition: Trace exosphere only: O₂ (~42%), Na (~29%), H₂ (~22%), He (~6%), K (~0.5%), trace H₂O, Ar, CO₂
surface_composition: Silicate rock and regolith; high-iron basalts; Mg-rich silicates (~35%), feldspar (~20%), pyroxene (~20%), olivine (~10%), iron sulfides (~5%), carbon (~1–3%)

name: Venus
surface_composition: Volcanic basalt; plagioclase feldspar (~35%), pyroxene (~30%), olivine (~15%), iron oxides (~10%), sulfur compounds (~5%), trace quartz and carbonates

name: Earth
surface_composition: 71% ocean (liquid water); continental crust: feldspar (~41%), quartz (~12%), pyroxene (~11%), mica (~5%), amphibole (~5%), iron/magnesium silicates; oceanic crust: basalt, gabbro

name: Mars
surface_composition: Iron(III) oxide dust/regolith (~15–30%); basaltic rock: pyroxene (~30%), feldspar (~25%), olivine (~10%), magnetite (~5%), perchlorate salts (~0.5–1%), trace sulfates and chlorides

name: Jupiter
atmospheric_composition: H₂ (~89.8%), He (~10.2%), CH₄ (~0.3%), NH₃ (~0.026%), HD (~0.003%), C₂H₂, C₂H₆, H₂O (trace, below cloud deck), phosphine (trace)
surface_composition: Gas giant — no solid surface; layers transition from gaseous H₂/He atmosphere → liquid metallic hydrogen (depth ~20,000 km) → possible rocky/icy core (~10–15 Earth masses) at center

name: Saturn
atmospheric_composition: H₂ (~96.3%), He (~3.25%), CH₄ (~0.45%), NH₃ (~0.0125%), HD (~0.011%), C₂H₂, C₂H₆, phosphine (trace), H₂O (trace, deep atmosphere)
surface_composition: Gas giant — no solid surface; atmosphere transitions to liquid metallic hydrogen at depth; possible rocky/icy core (~9–22 Earth masses); rings composed of 90–95% water ice particles (cm to meters), ~5–10% rocky debris

name: Uranus
atmospheric_composition: H₂ (~82.5%), He (~15.2%), CH₄ (~2.3%), HD (~0.009%), C₂H₂, C₂H₆ (trace); CH₄ ice clouds give blue-green color
surface_composition: Ice giant — no solid surface; "icy" mantle of water (H₂O), ammonia (NH₃), and methane (CH₄) ices (~60–70% by mass) surrounding a small rocky silicate/iron core (~20% by mass)

name: Neptune
atmospheric_composition: H₂ (~80%), He (~19%), CH₄ (~1.5%), HD (~0.019%), C₂H₂, C₂H₆ (trace); CH₄ absorption gives deep blue color
surface_composition: Ice giant — no solid surface; mantle of water, ammonia, and methane ices under extreme pressure (~65% by mass); small rocky silicate/iron core (~25% by mass); ionic "hot ice" ocean likely present at depth

name: Moon
atmospheric_composition: Tenuous exosphere only: Ar (~70%), He (~29%), Ne, H₂, CO₂, CH₄ (all trace); Na and K detected near surface
surface_composition: Regolith and rock: plagioclase feldspar (~43%), pyroxene (~25%), olivine (~8%), ilmenite (~8%), glass/agglutinates (~10%); highlands: anorthosite; maria: Fe/Ti-rich basalt; trace H₂O ice at poles

name: Phobos
atmospheric_composition: None — no atmosphere; micrometeorite gardening produces thin transient dust
surface_composition: Carbonaceous chondrite-like regolith; phyllosilicates (~30%), olivine (~15%), pyroxene (~15%), carbon-rich material (~20%), fine dust/regolith (~20%); Stickney crater exposes brighter interior material

name: Deimos
atmospheric_composition: None — no atmosphere; smoother surface than Phobos due to thick regolith blanket
surface_composition: Similar to C-type carbonaceous chondrite; carbon-rich silicates (~40%), fine-grained regolith (~30%), phyllosilicates (~15%), pyroxene (~10%); much smoother than Phobos due to thick dust blanket

name: Io
atmospheric_composition: SO₂ (~90%), SO (~10%), NaCl, KCl, S₂, Cl (trace); atmosphere collapses when Io enters Jupiter's shadow
surface_composition: Most volcanically active body in solar system; SO₂ frost/snow (~30%), elemental sulfur allotropes (~40%, gives yellow/orange/red/black colors), silicate lava flows and basalt (~25%), NaCl and KCl deposits (~5%)

name: Europa
atmospheric_composition: O₂ (~100% of tenuous atmosphere); trace H₂O, H₂, H₂O₂; produced by radiolysis of surface ice by Jupiter's radiation belts
surface_composition: Water ice crust (~10–30 km thick); surface: H₂O ice (~80%), hydrated salts (MgSO₄, NaCl, ~15%), radiation-processed organics and sulfur compounds (~5%); reddish-brown linea likely briny material from subsurface ocean

name: Ganymede
atmospheric_composition: O₂ (~90%), O₃ (~10%), H₂O, H₂ (trace); tenuous atmosphere produced by sublimation and radiolysis of surface ice
surface_composition: Mixed ice and rock; H₂O ice (~50%), silicate rock (pyroxene, olivine, ~35%), carbon-rich dark material (~10%), MgSO₄ and other salts (~5%); dark ancient terrain (sulci) interspersed with younger grooved terrain

name: Callisto
atmospheric_composition: CO₂ (~100% of tenuous atmosphere); trace O₂ and H₂; CO₂ likely sublimating from dry ice deposits
surface_composition: Most heavily cratered object in the solar system; roughly equal mix of H₂O ice (~40%) and dark rocky/carbonaceous material (~40%); CO₂ ice (~10%), sulfur compounds (~5%), tholins and organic residue (~5%)

name: Titan
atmospheric_composition: N₂ (~94–98%), CH₄ (~1.4–5.6%), H₂ (~0.1%), Ar (~0.004%), trace C₂H₂, C₂H₄, C₂H₆, HCN, CO, CO₂; thick orange haze of tholins (complex organics)
surface_composition: Water ice bedrock beneath thick organic (tholin) sediment layer; liquid methane/ethane lakes and seas near poles; dunes of solid organic particles (~40%), water ice crust (~35%), organic sand and sediment (~20%), liquid CH₄/C₂H₆ (polar regions)

name: Enceladus
atmospheric_composition: H₂O (~91%), N₂ (~4%), CO₂ (~3.2%), CH₄ (~1.7%), H₂ (~0.8%), NH₃, H₂S (trace); vented directly from subsurface ocean via south polar geysers
surface_composition: Brightest object in solar system; nearly pure H₂O ice surface (~95%); sodium chloride (NaCl) and silica nanoparticles (~3%) detected in plumes; organic compounds (~2%) detected; south polar region fractured "tiger stripes" vent subsurface ocean

name: Triton
atmospheric_composition: N₂ (~99%), CH₄ (~0.01%), CO (trace); extremely tenuous; surface pressure ~14 microbars
surface_composition: N₂ ice (~55%, seasonal frost), CO ice (~15%), CO₂ ice (~10%), CH₄ ice (~10%), H₂O ice bedrock (~8%), dark tholins/organics (~2%); active N₂ geysers at south pole

name: Pluto
atmospheric_composition: N₂ (~97%), CH₄ (~2.5%), CO (~0.5%); thin haze layers of tholins up to 200 km altitude; atmosphere partially collapses when Pluto moves away from Sun
surface_composition: Sputnik Planitia (N₂ ice plain, ~30%); CH₄ ice deposits (~25%); H₂O ice bedrock (~25%); CO ice (~10%); tholins/dark red organics (~8%); rocky silicate interior beneath icy shell

name: Ceres
atmospheric_composition: Transient water vapor only; localized outgassing near bright spots (Occator Crater); no permanent atmosphere
surface_composition: Carbonaceous chondrite-like; phyllosilicates/clays (~30%), Mg/Ca carbonates (~25%), ammoniated clays (~20%), sodium carbonate and NaCl (bright Occator spots, ~10%), dark carbon-rich material (~10%), H₂O ice (polar shadows, ~5%)

name: Eris
atmospheric_composition: Collapsed N₂/CH₄ atmosphere when near aphelion (currently frozen); transient thin N₂/CH₄ atmosphere possible near perihelion
surface_composition: Nearly uniform bright surface: CH₄ ice (~50%), N₂ ice (~30%), H₂O ice bedrock (~15%), trace tholins (~5%); one of the most reflective known bodies

name: Makemake
atmospheric_composition: No detected global atmosphere; possible localized CH₄ sublimation near equator; atmosphere likely collapses to surface frost at current distance
surface_composition: CH₄ ice (~70%, gives reddish tint from irradiation), ethane (C₂H₆) ice (~15%), N₂ ice (~10%), tholins/dark organics (~5%); surface dominated by large CH₄ ice grains

name: Haumea
atmospheric_composition: None; extremely rapid rotation (3.9 hr) and elongated shape prevent atmosphere retention; no outgassing detected
surface_composition: Nearly pure crystalline H₂O ice (~80%); dark red organic/carbon-rich spot (~15%, Yamamoto feature); trace CH₄ or NH₃ hydrates (~5%); rapid spin creates oblate/triaxial ellipsoid shape; has a ring system discovered in 2017

name: Vesta
atmospheric_composition: None; transient OH detected possibly from solar wind interaction with surface minerals; no permanent atmosphere
surface_composition: Differentiated asteroid; howardite-eucrite-diogenite (HED) basalts; pyroxene (~40%), feldspar (~25%), olivine (~10%), impact melt glass (~15%), opaque minerals (ilmenite, troilite, ~10%); large Rheasilvia impact basin dominates south pole

name: Bennu
atmospheric_composition: None; OSIRIS-REx mission detected particle ejection events (cm-sized rocks). No atmosphere, but active surface processes
surface_composition: B-type carbonaceous chondrite; hydrated silicates/phyllosilicates (~40%), carbon-rich material (~30%), magnetite (~15%), olivine and pyroxene (~10%), organics (~5%); OSIRIS-REx sample return (2023) confirmed abundant carbon and water-bearing minerals

name: Psyche
atmospheric_composition: None; possible transient OH from solar wind sputtering; NASA Psyche spacecraft arrived 2023 for detailed study
surface_composition: Likely exposed metallic core of differentiated protoplanet; iron-nickel metal (~30–60%), pyroxene silicates (~20–40%), olivine (~10%), sulfides (troilite, pyrrhotite, ~10%); lower-than-expected density suggests mix of metal and silicate rather than pure metal
